headlines.article_text: U.S. eyes Reliance’s refining muscle for Western crude as Rubio visits Jamnagar plant Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. is looking to work with Reliance Industries for refining Western energy supplies. Rubio is visiting Reliance's Jamnagar refinery, which is the world's "largest and most complex single-site refinery" with crude processing capacity of 1.4 million barrels per day. Rubio underscored Reliance's ability to refine heavy crude and referred to India as a "refining superpower" when asked about the role the country can play in meeting the world's energy demand. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks during the Freedom 250 reception at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on October 20, 2026. Kylie Cooper | Afp | Getty Images U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will discuss refining Western energy supplies with Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries when he visits the company's plant in Jamnagar, Gujarat — the world's largest single-site refinery. The U.S. is looking to "work together more closely" with Reliance for refining energy from the "Western Hemisphere," Rubio said in an interview with India's Network 18, which is owned by Reliance. "I think that's helpful to India, but it's also helpful to us," he added. Reliance's Jamnagar refinery, which Rubio will visit on Wednesday, has a crude processing capacity of 1.4 million barrels per day. Reliance has also emerged as the biggest buyer of Venezuelan crude outside of the U.S., as of end-September. The company's "extraordinary" refining capacity could help India diversify its energy supplies, Rubio said, hinting at possibly greater offtake of Venezuelan crude. "We think there's an opportunity for them [Reliance Industries] to continue to help India diversify its supply chain, its supply of energy," Rubio said, adding that Venezuela was ramping up energy production, and that "India has had a long history of being able to refine some of that." U.S. President Donald Trump has been pushing India to buy more Venezuelan oil to replace Russian barrels, and while state-owned oil companies are making opportunistic purchases, Reliance has been the primary buyer. 'Refining Superpower' Beyond oil purchases, Reliance has been deepening ties with the U.S. this year, with Trump announcing in March that America will build its first new oil refinery in 50 years, helped by investment from Ambani's Reliance. While Reliance has not confirmed the size of investment, Trump in a Truth Social post had said that "THIS IS A HISTORIC $300 BILLION DOLLAR DEAL — THE BIGGEST IN U.S. HISTORY." Reliance has never made an announcement about the refinery investment, Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, South Asia practice head at Eurasia Group, told CNBC, adding that it creates an air of uncertainty around the deal. Rubio would seek to "clinch" that deal or take it a little further, Chaudhuri said. Rubio told Network 18 that Reliance had "invested in increasing the refining capacity within the United States." His visit to Jamnagar also comes at a time when diesel prices have surged in the U.S., with midterm elections looming. headlines.article_text: SpaceX (SPCX) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 2:20 02:20 SpaceX earnings in focus as Starlink growth and AI spending take center stage Morning Call SpaceX shares climbed about 8% in extended trading on Tuesday after the company reported 161% revenue growth for the third quarter, beating Wall Street estimates, with its artificial intelligence business growing ninefold. On the earnings call, CEO Elon Musk said a merger with Tesla , his automaker, would be a "good idea," adding that the boards of both companies have formed special committees to discuss a tie-up. Tesla reports third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Here's how SpaceX did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: Revenue: $14.58 billion vs. $12.72 billion expected Earnings per share: 45 cents adjusted vs. 13 cents expected SpaceX said in a release that it recorded operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion. In the same period a year earlier, SpaceX reported a net loss of $1.05 billion. CFO Bret Johnsen said on the call that revenue in the first quarter of 2027 will be $33 billion to $37 billion, trouncing the average $22.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. Johnsen attributed the forecast to "increased visibility into our compute contract pipeline over the next six months." While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service. Starlink's subscribers base grew to 13.6 million in the quarter, up from 12 million in the prior period. Total connectivity revenue jumped 69% to $5.25 billion from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Analysts were expecting $4.84 billion, according to StreetAccount. Revenue from consumer Starlink subscribers amounted to $3.12 billion, while the company generated $2.13 billion from government and enterprise customers. Buzz has been building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. mobile network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation. SpaceX jumped into AI with the purchase earlier this year of xAI, Musk's AI lab. The company has been rapidly expanding that business by renting out capacity to Google , Anthropic and others. AI, which SpaceX now calls "Super Intelligence," has emerged as its largest business. Revenue jumped ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Analysts expected sales of $6.47 billion, according to StreetAccount. During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor. Meanwhile, SpaceX's launch business was up just slightly in the quarter, with sales rising to $1.77 billion from $1.67 billion a year ago. Almost all of SpaceX's profit still comes from Starlink. Operating income in the connectivity unit about doubled to $2.37 billion. The AI business swung to a profit of $431 million, while the space division lost $7 million. Between infrastructure, cloud deals and paying users of the Grok AI models and products, Musk said on the call that annual recurring revenue by the end of next year will be between $500 billion and $1 trillion. Analysts are projecting full-year 2027 revenue of about $110 billion, according to LSEG, which would be up more than 100% from this year. 5 Hours Ago SpaceX generated revenue of $1.77 billion from launches watch now VIDEO 5:47 05:47 SpaceX shares continue to climb on Q3 beat Fast Money SpaceX's launch business generated $1.77 billion in revenue in the third quarter. The company touted its Starship Flight 14 as a major milestone on the earnings call, and Musk said SpaceX will attempt to "catch both the booster and the ship," during its next test flight of the massive rocket. He added that SpaceX has a "steady stream of Starship flight attempts" scheduled through the end of this year, and accelerating next year. The company recently announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said on the call that SpaceX aims to conduct its first launch from the facility by 2029. Musk said the first launch may be possible by the end of 2028. 5 Hours Ago SpaceX must face NAACP lawsuit over air pollution in Memphis area The U.S. Department of Justice lost its bid to have a federal court in Mississippi toss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP against SpaceX alleging Clean Air Act violations by Musk's company in the Memphis area. The DOJ had accused the NAACP of threatening "American national, economic, and energy security" by asking the court to temporarily shut off of the power supply used by SpaceX at its Colossus data centers. The data centers are powered by methane gas-burning turbines, installed by SpaceX's AI business. The NAACP, in its suit, said Musk's company built and used gas-burning turbines for power without first obtaining proper permits, and without installing required pollution controls. In the court's order, published Tuesday , a judge wrote there was "no 'fairly possible' interpretation of the Clean Air Act that would give the United States the right to unilaterally dismiss a citizen suit." 8 Hours Ago Musk says Tesla-SpaceX merger would be 'good idea' A fleet of Tesla Cyber trucks is parked at charging stations outside the SpaceX launch production facility in Starbase, Texas, U.S., July 20, 2026. Because Musk is a "conflicted party," he said he can't be in the discussions. "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said, referring to the development of software, chips and more. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said. "But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this." Musk said that on the Tesla side, "we will need a 50% vote of all shares -- not just those who vote -- but of all shareholders, and that's quite a high hurdle."
